text.p: Italian luxury goods firm Gucci Group NV posted record annual profits Thursday and said it was set for its next growth phase.
Net income for fiscal 1996 more than doubled to $168.4 million from $82.9 million in fiscal 1995.
Gucci, listed on stock exchanges in New York and Amsterdam, said the results were buoyed by record performances across the board, in distribution, product categories and geographic regions.
The company designs, makes and distributes luxury accessories, including leather goods, shoes, watches, jewelry and perfume.
"We continue to be confident of growth in Italy and the rest of the world for 1997," said Gucci Chairman Domenico De Sole in a video news conference from Toyko with journalists in Milan.
Revenues for fiscal 1996 increased 76.1 percent to $880.7 million vs. a previous $500.1 million.
Sales for directly-operated stores rose by more than 60 percent, while wholesale, including franchise, duty free and department & speciality stores, soared by over 180 percent.
Net income per share rose to $2.76 from $1.68.
Gross profit margins for the year slipped to 64.5 percent from 65.9 percent in 1995.

This year Gucci plans to expand and refurbish its flagship stores in London's Sloane Street and in Beverly Hills, Calif., giving them a "cleaner, more modern look which is consistent with the image of our brand," the company said.
De Sole said the group's first two stores in China had opened in February and the outlets in Beijing and Shanghai had started well in their first few weeks of trading.

Gucci has been one of the most remarkable corporate recovery stories in Italy. Founded by Guccio Gucci in Florence in 1923, it underwent serious problems in the late 1970s and the 1980s as a third generation of Gucci cousins quarreled among themselves.

Bahrain-based Investcorp bought up Gucci in two steps in 1989 and 1993 and turned the company rapidly around by gaining more control of its distribution and refocusing the group under a new U.S. designer Tom Ford. Investcorp completed the full stock flotation of the group in early 1996.
Gucci stock was up $1.50 to $72.375 in early afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
